Genetic subtype of immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease; no additional common organ damage established.
Axial skeletal dysplasia; retinal dystrophy and progressive visual loss occur in >90%. Restrictive ventilatory defect reported in 2/11, below threshold.
Neoplasm originates in the nasal cavity, an upper airway site. Lymphoma is only one subtype.
Inherited retinal degeneration causing congenital visual impairment; optic disc abnormalities remain within the ocular axis.
Somatoform psychiatric disorder without a specified directly damaged organ.
Renal hypodysplasia and optic nerve dysplasia define the syndrome. Scoliosis reported in 2/4 supports skeletal involvement, though evidence is limited; hypertension is secondary to renal disease.
Inborn bile acid synthesis defect defined by neonatal cholestasis and impaired intestinal fat absorption.
Bradykinin-mediated angioedema predominantly affects skin and oral tissues, especially tongue. Normal-C1-inhibitor PLG disease is not an immunodeficiency; airway attacks are a minority.
Defining hypotrichosis, vascular/lymphatic malformations and renal defects. Developmental delay is occasional; pulmonary lymphangiectasia has no established common frequency.
Defining gonadotropin deficiency. Anosmia/hyposmia reported in 2/8 and hearing impairment in 2/8, both below 30%.
Isolated developmental abnormality of the cornea and anterior eye segment; associated complications remain ocular.
Schizophrenia is a psychiatric disorder without an axis. Listed congenital anomalies lack evidence of common direct organ involvement.
Defining urethral hypospadias and laryngotracheoesophageal defects; dysphagia 6/7. Developmental delay occurs in 19/37 (~51%), with CNS malformations supporting neurologic involvement.
Idiopathic immune-mediated inflammation of the uvea, retina and vitreous; no established extraocular disease.
Inherited macular and cone-rod degeneration causing visual loss.
Bone fragility and defective mineralization define this skeletal disorder. Blue sclerae do not establish ocular damage; motor delay reflects skeletal disease.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss confined to the auditory system.
Malignant bone-forming tumour arising from the bone surface; metastatic risks do not establish additional involvement.
Bacterial infection directly damages the inner-ear labyrinth. Meningitis may be the source, rather than an intrinsic manifestation.
Defining polyneuropathy/intellectual disability, short-limb skeletal abnormalities and premature ovarian endocrine failure. Arrhythmia is occasional.
Ectodermal defects, hypothyroidism and airway ciliary dysfunction define disease; enteropathy is a defining manifestation. Ocular findings omitted at cap; tear abnormalities alone lack clear damage.
Genetic focal epilepsy affects cerebral function; seizure auras do not establish separate ocular or otologic damage.
Primary intraventricular central nervous system tumour.
Congenital distal contractures define disease. Eyelid ptosis occurs in 5/15 (~33%). Cleft palate is occasional; high palate alone does not establish functional damage.
